## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.23 — New icon, 26 languages, right-to-left

### A new icon

Six coloured strands sweeping into a single node — many hues in, one output,
which is what the app does and what "mux" in the name means. It replaces a
stock Android system drawable that no store would have accepted.

### The app speaks 26 languages

Every string is translated into 25 languages besides English, including Arabic,
Japanese, Korean, both Chinese scripts, Hindi, and separate variants for
Spanish (Spain / Latin America), Portuguese (Brazil / Portugal) and French
(France / Canada).

Pick one in **Settings → Language**. Each language is listed in its own
language, so it can be found without being able to read the rest of the UI.

**These are machine translations.** They are structurally checked — no missing
strings, no broken substitutions — but nobody has read them for quality.
Corrections are very welcome on the issue tracker.

Arabic mirrors the whole layout. There is a **Text direction** setting next to
the language for forcing the mirrored layout in any language, which exists so
the mirroring can be checked without reading Arabic.

### Settings

- **Changes apply as you make them.** The Save button is gone. It was a second
  step that existed only to be forgotten, and it misreported failure: one save
  for the whole form made a rejected field look as though nothing had been
  stored, when nothing had been *sent*.
- **The options are words now**, not raw values — "Lights only" rather than
  "lights", "Self-signed certificate" rather than "selfsigned".
- Buttons and fields look like the rest of the app.

### The pairing screen looked like two different screens

It is one component, but it rendered with filled blue buttons on Sync and plain
grey ones on Lights, because only one of those pages loaded the stylesheet that
styled buttons. There is now one button style across the whole app.

### Also

The app has a favicon in the browser for the first time, and the About section
shows the version you actually installed rather than the word "android".
